description.narrative: ForumCiv syftar med programmet att bidra till ökad tillgång till land för kvinnor och unga, samt stärka civilsamhället i Liberia. I ett längre perspektiv kan detta leda till ökad social sammanhållning och motverka konflikt i landet. Det övergripande målet för insatsens är att "Kvinnor och unga i rurala samhällen i Bomi, Bong and Grand Gedeh aktivt deltar i markförvaltning och reglering, samt har tillgång till ägarskap och kontroll av deras mark för hållbar utveckling och motståndskraft mot klimatförändringar." med fyra förväntade resultat, 1) stärkt kapacitet hos ForumCiv i Liberia och deras partner; 2) ökad medvetenhet om landsförvaltning; 3) målgrupperna utvecklar sina egna strategier för tillgång till och ägarskap av land; 4) dialog och partnerskap mellan civilsamhället och andra aktörer.

ForumCiv’s programme aims to contribute to increased access to land for women and youth and strengthen civil society in Liberia. In a longer perspective, this can lead to increased social cohesion and prevent conflict in the country. The main objective of the programme is that “Women and youth from rural communities in Bomi, Bong and Grand Gedeh counties effectively participate in land governance and management, and access ownership and control of their land for sustainable development and resilience to climate change.” Expecting four outcomes, 1) improving capacity of ForumCiv's office and partners; 2) increased awareness on land governance; 3) target groups developing their own strategies for access and land ownership; 4) dialogue and partnerships between civil society and other actors.

Objective Women and youth from rural communities in Bomi, Bong and Grand Gedeh counties effectively participate in land governance and management, and access ownership and control of their land for sustainable development and resilience to climate change.

description.narrative:
Examples of results from the first two years of implementation include:
- Community conflicts, including long-standing land disputes, resolved through the Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanism by ForumCiv's partners, after organising trainings on ADR with the Ministry of Justice.
- 24 rural women became landowners in customary communities following awareness and advocacy actions by partners.
- Two womens associations in Bomi, with a total of 143 members, were given land by local leaders because of their advocacy. The women can now use the land for farming, and the members, who are mostly single mothers, rely on the proceeds from the sales of the harvest to sustain their homes and children.
- 25 community-based structures for supporting management and governance of customary lands have been established. These have a combined membership of 727 persons, and women and youth are playing increasing roles in management of customary lands through these structures, with women and youth making out 65 % of members and 45 % of leadership. These community structures are involved in advocacy to promote land rights of women and youth, and monitor movement and activities of forest users.
- Disbursement of grants to 15 community-based partner organisations in 3 counties, enabled the partners to set up community based structures to lead and advocate for human rights, democracy, gender equality and land rights of women and youth, the sustainable use of natural resources, and fight SGBV.
- Three clans and six communities engaged in the Community Land formalisation process have been supported in setting up community land management committees, organise boundary harmonisation exercises and engage with Liberia Land Authority and land surveyors.
